Article Text:

Steps to download Minecraft Bedrock 26.50.22 beta and preview

Article Title: After hacking into world's biggest repository of AI models Hugging Face, OpenAI's rogue AI agent 'attacked' another tech company
Article Text:
Modal Labs says OpenAI's rogue agent exploited its customer code

Modal Labs says customer code, not its platform, was exploited



OpenAI says rogue AI accessed four accounts

The rogue AI agent that carried out a cyberattack on AI platform Hugging Face also compromised a customer hosted by another technology company, Modal Labs, reports Reuters citing a company executive and sources familiar with the matter. The latest details suggest the OpenAI-tested AI agent reached more systems than previously known during its hacking spree earlier this month. While Modal said its own platform was not breached, the incident has raised fresh questions about the risks of autonomous AI systems after the agent exploited vulnerable code before launching a wider attack on Hugging Face, according to a Reuters report.According to a timeline published by Hugging Face on Tuesday, the rogue AI agent first broke into a sandbox, or an isolated testing environment, hosted on a third-party provider's infrastructure before using it to launch the broader attack.Modal's Chief Technology Officer Akshat Bubna confirmed to Reuters that the third-party provider was Modal. He said the AI agent exploited vulnerable code written by one of Modal's customers that was hosted on the company's platform.According to Modal, the customer had "published an unauthenticated endpoint that allowed anyone on the internet to use their sandboxes for code execution," effectively leaving a system open to attackers."Modal's platform or isolation were not compromised in any way," Bubna said.OpenAI declined to comment specifically on the Modal incident. Instead, it referred the news agency to an update in which it said the rogue AI agent had broken into four accounts across four separate services.While the company did not identify those services, a person familiar with the matter identified Modal as one of them, says Reuters report.OpenAI also said it had not found "any other activity at the level of severity or scale of what we've shared related to Hugging Face, which involved a platform-level compromise."
Article Summary: Rogue AI agent that attacked AI platform Hugging Face also compromised a customer hosted by another technology company, reports Reuters. The latest details suggest the OpenAI-tested AI agent reached more systems than previously known. While Modal said its own platform was not breached, the incident has raised fresh questions about the risks of autonomous AI systems.

Article Title: American billionaire Mark Cuban to CEOs: Stop getting ‘shocked’ by healthcare costs, turn to your HR Head as HR is …
Article Text:
Hidden costs in healthcare contracts



AI as a solution



Read Mark Cuban’s complete post here



CEOs turn to their Head of HR. HR is understaffed. They are being asked to take care of all their employees and families and all the issues associated with keeping them as healthy and sane and productive give as possible.

It’s an impossible job.

When I talk to that Head of HR, they say they have to trust the big insurance carriers who are their ASO and PBM. They have no choice but to

On one hand their members are terrified to change their insurance carriers for fear of losing their doctor, or other continuity issues

The vertically integrated conglomerates that own the ASO, PBM, ClearingHouse and so many more companies that have contracts with the employer , know they are afraid to change , so they take advantage

Even when that employer uses a consultant or broker , there is probably a 50pct or greater chance the broker/consultant doesn’t want to go through the work of changing, they would rather collect their fees and not change.

There are even reporting requirements (Form 5500) to disclose these costs, but the ceo has no clue about them.

All this leads to lack of change. Even when every penny they save goes right to the bottom line and increases their stock price

What I told a ceo today ? Take a off of all of your healthcare contracts and put it in your Claude , ChatGPT, grok, Gemini, whatever and use this prompt

“Where are they ripping me off “

They are always shocked.

American billionaire and entrepreneur Mark Cuban has urged the US CEOs to rethink how they manage employee healthcare, warning that executives are overspending because they lack visibility into complex insurance contracts. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Cuban said leaders often turn to their HR leads, who are “understaffed” and overwhelmed. “They are being asked to take care of all their employees and families and all the issues associated with keeping them as healthy and sane and productive as possible,” he wrote.Cuban also argued that vertically integrated conglomerates which own administrative service organisations (ASOs), pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), and clearinghouses — exploit employers’ reluctance to switch providers. Brokers and consultants, he added, often discourage changes because of the extra work involved. “The vertically integrated conglomerates… know they are afraid to change, so they take advantage,” Cuban said.Cuban recommended CEOs use AI tools to review healthcare contracts and uncover hidden costs. “What I told a CEO today? Take all of your healthcare contracts and put it in your Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Gemini, whatever and use this prompt: ‘Where are they ripping me off?’ They are always shocked,” he wrote.
Article Summary: CEOs are overspending because they lack visibility into complex insurance contracts, says Mark Cuban. Cuban said leaders often turn to their HR leads, who are ‘understaffed’ and overwhelmed. “The vertically integrated conglomerates… know they are afraid to change, so they take advantage,” Cuban said.

Article Title: ITC Infotech partners with Google Cloud to drive agentic AI transformation
Article Text:
Google Cloud

The enterprise-wide rollout spans multiple functions:

Accelerated software engineering: Optimizing development velocity, managing legacy code migration, and speeding modernization.

Autonomous workflows: Deploying multi-agent orchestration to execute complex corporate tasks securely.

Corporate function automation: Streamlining HR, finance, legal, and IT processes, from RFP drafting to invoice audits.

ITC Infotech has announced a strategic partnership with Google Cloud to accelerate enterprise-wide agentic transformation and AI innovation. The Bangalore-based technology services provider will become “customer zero” for Google’s Gemini Enterprise, deploying the platform across its operations before rolling out proven methodologies and blueprints to global customers.By embedding Gemini Enterprise into its own workflows, ITC Infotech aims to validate and scale autonomous AI capabilities internally. CEO Manas Chakraborty said: “Our wall-to-wall deployment of Gemini Enterprise anchors our agentic-first strategy, driving non-linear, AI-led progress for our business. It ensures we build deep operational expertise and proprietary IP to deliver next-generation outcomes for customers worldwide. ”Beyond internal transformation, ITC Infotech and Google Cloud will establish Joint Centers of Excellence to serve as innovation hubs. These CoEs will develop industry-specific AI blueprints and frameworks for sectors including consumer packaged goods, retail, hospitality, and manufacturing.Sashi Sreedharan, Managing Director of Google Cloud India, said: “By standardizing its daily workflows on Google Cloud AI, ITC Infotech is gaining deep, practical experience with advanced automation at scale. Together, we are uniquely positioned to empower organizations worldwide to safely and effectively scale their own AI initiatives.”
Article Summary: ITC Infotech has announced a strategic partnership with Google Cloud to accelerate enterprise-wide agentic transformation and AI innovation. Bangalore- based technology services provider will become ‘customer zero’ for Google’s Gemini Enterprise. ITC Infotech aims to validate and scale autonomous AI capabilities internally.

Article Title: Microsoft AI chief Mustafa Suleyman sees a warning in Sam Altman's AI model hacking Hugging Face; says: They need to be handled ...
Article Text:
Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman

Race for cyber defense accelerates



Microsoft’s AI chief, Mustafa Suleyman, has dubbed a recent cyber incident involving a ‘runaway’ OpenAI agent as a major “warning shot” for the tech industry, emphasising the growing risks posed by autonomous artificial intelligence (AI). The Microsoft executive’s comments follow OpenAI’s recent admission that one of its autonomous AI agents slipped out of a controlled test environment and executed a multi-day cyberattack against the popular AI startup Hugging Face.Suleyman called the breach an “important lesson” for developers rushing to roll out increasingly capable models.“These are very powerful [tools] and they need to be handled incredibly carefully. And we need extreme attention to detail,” Suleyman said in an interview with the Financial Times, adding, “The precautionary principle is going to matter here as the models get more and more powerful and I think it’s a warning shot.”The Hugging Face breach has heightened concerns across Silicon Valley about AI’s potential to discover and exploit software vulnerabilities autonomously. Industry scrutiny has centred on Anthropic’s powerful Mythos model, released in April, as well as OpenAI's aggressive push to build competitive AI cyber tools.Microsoft executives argue that building stronger AI-driven defensive capabilities is the only way to safeguard systems against increasingly sophisticated threats.“Attackers have [these] models. So we have to evaluate and push so that the defenders can defend. It’s not like we have a choice,” said Hayete Gallot, Microsoft’s security chief.Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang talked about the hacking and converted the incident into an opportunity to bring the top AI labs together as ‘defenders’“Attackers have frontier AI. Defenders need a frontier AI ecosystem—the best open and closed models, force-multiplied by a global community,” Huang said in a post on X (formerly Twitter).“During the Hugging Face incident, closed AI blocked essential forensics. An open-weight frontier model helped contain the intrusion. That’s why we created the Open Secure AI Alliance,” he added.
Article Summary: Mustafa Suleyman, Microsoft's AI chief, has dubbed a recent cyber incident involving a ‘runaway’ OpenAI agent as a major ‘warning shot’ for the tech industry. OpenAI admitted that one of its autonomous AI agents slipped out of a controlled test environment and executed a multi-day cyberattack against the popular AI startup Hugging Face.

Article Title: Meta had pledged to be Net Zero by 2030, but the company has now seemingly changed its mind; exits climate group; here’s what pressured Facebook-parent
Article Text:
What likely made Meta to take a U-turn on its Climate commitment



How Apple, Google and Microsoft continue to stand by their 'climate promise'



Meta -- the company behind Facebook , Instagram and WhatsApp -- has reportedly withdrawn from the RE100 initiative after investments in new gas-fired power plants left the technology giant unable to meet the group’s renewable energy criteria. The decision reverses a commitment Meta made in 2020 to support a transition towards electricity generated entirely from renewable sources. Recharge first reported that Meta and RE100 had parted ways because the tech giant no longer met the initiative’s technical criteria. Meta joined RE100 as Facebook in 2016 and pledged to cover its entire operation with renewable electricity by 2020. The tech giant stated in 2021 that it had reached that target. Meta has always done so with renewable energy certificates (RECs) and PPAs, not by powering directly with renewables.RE100 is a global corporate initiative whose members commit to sourcing their electricity from renewable sources. Its members include Apple, Google and Microsoft. “After several in-depth conversations between Meta and Climate Group, Meta has withdrawn from the RE100 initiative, as it is no longer able to meet the technical criteria due to investments made in new gas power,” a Climate Group spokesperson said.It comes as the company expands its artificial intelligence infrastructure, including energy-intensive data centres.Meta has backed several gas-fired power projects to support its expanding data-centre operations. The company is working with Entergy Corp on plans for plants in Louisiana that would supply more than 5 gigawatts of electricity to its Richland Parish data centre.Analysts say that the move underscores the challenge technology companies face in securing reliable power for AI operations. The decision exposes a technology industry conflict. AI needs constant power, while renewable sources often require batteries or backup systems. AI Data centres require large and consistent supplies of electricity for computing, cooling and backup systems, while renewable projects can face intermittency, storage and grid-capacity constraints.Meta is not the only technology company looking beyond renewable energy to meet rising demand. Google and Microsoft have also invested in projects involving fossil fuels, although both continue to pursue clean-energy technologies. Microsoft has adopted an hourly energy-matching strategy intended to align electricity consumption with cleaner power generation. Google, meanwhile, is working with Form Energy on long-duration battery storage capable of supplying electricity for up to 100 hours.Gas-fired plants can generally be developed faster than nuclear facilities and provide more consistent electricity than intermittent renewable sources. However, Meta’s withdrawal is likely to raise further questions about whether the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure is undermining the technology industry’s earlier climate commitments.
Article Summary: Facebook-owned Meta has withdrawn from the RE100 initiative. The tech giant has backed several gas-fired power projects to support its expanding data-centre operations. Google and Microsoft have also invested in projects involving fossil fuels, although both continue to pursue clean-energy technologies.

Article Text:
What Anthropic said on the leaked chats of users

What went wrong

Privacy risks ahead

A trove of seemingly private conversations with Anthropic’s Claude chatbot appeared in Google Search results recently, sparking alarm after users discovered sensitive information including cryptocurrency wallet keys and personal details which have been exposed inadvertently. According to a report by Fortune, the issue was traced to Claude’s ‘share’ feature which enables users to generate a link to send a conversation to others.AI giant Anthropic said that the company itself did not make chats searchable, instead blaming the way users shared links. “We give people control over sharing their Claude conversations publicly, and in keeping with our privacy principles, we do not share chat directories or sitemaps with search engines like Google,” a spokesperson told Fortune. The company emphasised that links are only accessible if users choose to share them, but once shared, they can be archived by third-party services.As per the report by Fortune, members of a Reddit discussion channel has discovered that typing some search phrases in Google pulled up a long lists of shared Claude conversations and Claude Artifacts — itself did not make chats searchable, instead blaming the way users shared links.“We give people control over sharing their Claude conversations publicly, and in keeping with our privacy principles, we do not share chat directories or sitemaps with search engines like Google,” a spokesperson told Fortune. The company emphasized that links are only accessible if users choose to share them, but once shared, they can be archived by third-party services.Anthropic has since fixed the issue, removing the links from Google search, though previously shared URLs remain accessible to anyone who already has them. The incident is not unique: last year, a similar glitch exposed nearly 100,000 ChatGPT conversations, while Elon Musk’s Grok chatbot also suffered from the same vulnerability. The problem stems from how “share” features create unique URLs that can be indexed by search engines.Experts warn that shared chatbot conversations often contain more sensitive information than shared documents, since users treat AI assistants as places to “think out loud” about work, health, or legal issues. Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness.

Article Title: In 1934, this Pennsylvania mountain went from a hawk killing ground to the world's first raptor sanctuary and changed bird conservation forever
Article Text:
Why so many raptors pass over Hawk Mountain

When migration attracted hunters instead of birdwatchers

The birth of the world's first raptor sanctuary

The science behind Hawk Mountain's migration records

Which raptors can you see at Hawk Mountain

How to experience Hawk Mountain today

Every autumn, the skies above a forested ridge in eastern Pennsylvania fill with movement. Eagles drift on rising air, falcons streak across the horizon and kestrels appear in quick flashes before disappearing south. For generations, Hawk Mountain has been one of North America's best places to witness this seasonal migration because the landscape naturally funnels birds of prey along a narrow route through the Appalachian Mountains. Yet the ridge was not always known for conservation. Long before visitors arrived carrying binoculars and cameras, people climbed the same slopes with rifles.The transformation from a place where raptors were routinely shot to a protected sanctuary reshaped both bird conservation and the scientific study of migration, leaving a legacy that continues nearly a century later.Hawk Mountain sits within the Appalachian chain, where the shape of the landscape works in favour of migrating raptors. As birds travel between their breeding territories and wintering grounds, many avoid unnecessary effort by taking advantage of warm columns of rising air and favourable winds. The ridge creates ideal conditions for soaring flight, allowing large birds to cover long distances while using relatively little energy.That combination of geography and weather means thousands of raptors pass over the mountain during migration seasons. Some days bring only a steady trickle, while strong winds and good thermals can produce an almost continuous procession overhead. Visitors may watch bald eagles, broad-winged hawks, peregrine falcons and other species travelling within surprisingly close range.The conditions that concentrated birds also made Hawk Mountain attractive to hunters during the early twentieth century. Large numbers of raptors gathered in one place, creating easy targets as they crossed the ridge.At the time, birds of prey received little public sympathy. Hawks were widely viewed as pests because they hunted smaller birds and farm animals, and some government agencies even offered payments for certain species. Recreational shooting became common on the mountain, and many birds were killed during migration each year.Photographs showing piles of dead hawks eventually reached conservation campaigner Rosalie Edge in 1933. The images shocked her and convinced her that direct action was needed where official protection had failed.Rather than simply campaigning for stronger wildlife laws, Edge focused on saving the mountain itself. In 1934 she secured roughly 1,400 acres through a lease and appointed experienced bird enthusiasts Maurice and Irma Broun to live and work on the site.Their task was straightforward but demanding. They discouraged hunters, watched over the property and helped establish the area as a refuge instead of a shooting ground. Once the immediate threat had eased, the land was opened to visitors interested in observing migration rather than exploiting it.That decision marked the beginning of Hawk Mountain Sanctuary, recognised as the world's first sanctuary created specifically for birds of prey.Protection of the site quickly led to another lasting contribution. The Brouns began recording every migrating raptor they observed, producing a daily count that started in September 1934.The tradition never stopped. Staff members and volunteers continue the seasonal counts, creating what is regarded as the world's longest continuous record of migrating raptors. The information collected across decades allows scientists to compare annual changes in migration timing, population trends and species abundance.Modern technology has added another layer to this work. Satellite and GPS tracking now reveal where individual birds travel after leaving Hawk Mountain, complementing observations made from the lookout points. Together, the long-running counts and electronic tracking provide a clearer picture of migration routes across North America.Sixteen different species of raptors are regularly recorded at Hawk Mountain. Among the best known are the bald eagle and golden eagle, both large soaring birds that often attract the biggest crowds during migration.Smaller hunters also appear in good numbers. American kestrels, North America's smallest falcons, pass through alongside peregrine falcons, while hawks, vultures and harriers add to the seasonal variety. The exact mix changes through the migration period because different species travel at different times.During spring, from early April to the middle of May, roughly a thousand birds of prey are typically counted. Autumn is far busier. Between the middle of August and the middle of December, seasonal totals average around 18,000 migrating raptors.Migration remains the main reason people travel to Hawk Mountain, with spring and autumn offering the greatest chance of seeing birds overhead. Windy days generally produce the most active flights because stronger air currents help soaring birds continue their journey.The sanctuary has developed facilities for visitors while keeping its conservation purpose intact. South Lookout, one of its principal viewing areas, is wheelchair accessible, allowing more people to experience the migration.Nearly a century after Rosalie Edge acted to stop the annual killing, the same ridge tells a very different story. Instead of marking the end of countless migrations, Hawk Mountain has become a place where birds pass safely overhead and where generations of observations continue to improve understanding of North America's raptors.
Article Summary: Hawk Mountain Sanctuary is the world's first sanctuary created specifically for birds of prey. Visitors can watch bald eagles, broad-winged hawks, peregrine falcons and other species travelling within surprisingly close range. Sixteen different species of raptors are regularly recorded at Hawk Mountain.

Article Title: In 1929, Hawaii introduced Japanese white-eyes to control insects; they became its most abundant land bird and began competing with native birds for food
Article Text:
A courting pair of Japanese White-eyes (Zosterops japonicus) - Kauai, Hawaii. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons.

A bird brought in to fight insect pests

The competition was over food

In 1929, Hawaii introduced a small bird from Japan to help control insect pests. The Japanese white-eye, also known as the mejiro. Image Credits: Wikimedia Commons.

When a biological-control measure becomes part of the problem

In 1929, Hawaii introduced a small bird from Japan to help control insect pests. The Japanese white-eye, also known as the mejiro, was brought to the islands because officials hoped it would feed on insects harmful to agriculture. Instead, the bird spread rapidly, established itself across the archipelago and became one of Hawaii's most abundant land birds.Its success, however, created a new ecological concern. As Japanese white-eyes became widespread, they began using many of the same food resources as native Hawaiian birds. Research later suggested that this competition placed additional pressure on native species already threatened by habitat loss, introduced predators and disease.According to a study published by Yale University , Japanese white-eye (Zosterops japonicus) was introduced into Oahu in 1929 through the efforts of Hawaii's Board of Commissioners of Agriculture and Forestry with the intention of using the bird to control insect pests as a biological agent. The bird proved to be highly adaptable to its surroundings. Japanese white-eyes feed on insects, fruits and nectar and have adapted to a variety of habitats including forest and agricultural environments.Once established, the birds spread across the islands. Their ability to exploit different food sources and habitats helped them become one of the most common birds in the Hawaiian Islands. It fed on fruit and helped disperse seeds, becoming deeply integrated into the islands' ecosystems.As the species became more widespread, its interactions with native wildlife attracted increasing scientific attention. Researchers have found that Japanese white-eyes forage on a wide range of flowering plants and fruits while also consuming insects, making them an important part of Hawaii's present-day bird communities. Their ecological role, however, is not straightforward.The concern was not that Japanese white-eyes attacked native birds directly. Instead, they could compete with them by exploiting similar food sources and feeding in the same parts of plants. Research published in Ecological Monographs found evidence of negative associations between Japanese white-eyes and several native Hawaiian forest birds. The researchers reported patterns consistent with competition involving species such as the ‘I‘iwi and ‘Elepaio, although they also noted that the effects varied between species and locations.A later study published in Current Biology provided further evidence of the pressure created by the introduced bird. Researchers examined Japanese white-eyes and eight native Hawaiian passerines and found substantial overlap in the resources and locations used for foraging. They also found that, after 2000, juveniles of every native species examined had lower body mass in areas where white-eye abundance had increased. Many also had shorter bills and tarsi, while smaller body size was associated with reduced survival in several species. During the same period, the endangered Hawai‘i ‘Akepa population was judged to have become non-viable. The findings suggested that competition did not have to involve direct aggression. When two species rely on similar resources, an abundant introduced species can gain an advantage simply by consuming or occupying the same resources as native birds.The Japanese white-eye's success in Hawaii illustrates how an introduced species can become part of an ecosystem in ways that extend beyond its original purpose. The birds compete with some native species for food, while their fruit-eating habits also allow them to disperse seeds as they move between plants. One further complication is that the white-eye's ecological role can vary depending on the habitat and species it encounters. By moving between fragmented patches of vegetation, the bird can connect areas that might otherwise remain isolated, while its feeding behaviour can influence which plants spread across the landscape. The species' history also highlights one of the challenges associated with biological control. Once an introduced animal establishes a breeding population, it can spread and interact with native species in ways that may not have been anticipated.The white-eye's presence is not the sole explanation for the pressures faced by Hawaii's native birds, which are affected by several environmental threats. But its spread shows how an introduction intended to serve one purpose can have wider ecological consequences.
Article Summary: Japanese white-eye (Zosterops japonicus) was introduced into Oahu in 1929 through the efforts of Hawaii's Board of Commissioners of Agriculture and Forestry with the intention of using the bird to control insect pests. The bird proved to be highly adaptable to its surroundings. It fed on fruit and helped disperse seeds, becoming deeply integrated into the islands' ecosystems. As the species became more widespread, its interactions with native wildlife attracted increasing scientific attention.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael Faraday: 'There's nothing quite as frightening as someone who knows they are right' and how blind certainty is human nature's most dangerous trap
Article Text:
'There's nothing quite as frightening as someone who knows they are right'

"There's nothing quite as frightening as someone who knows they are right,

The self-taught genius who questioned everything

The psychological trap of total conviction

Unyielding mindsets in everyday life

The virtue of staying open

A room full of clever people falls silent when someone speaks with total confidence. Doubt creates space for discussion, compromise, and checking the facts. Absolute certainty does the exact opposite. It shuts down debate, ignores warning signs, and treats any disagreement as a personal attack." warned the 19th-century scientist Michael Faraday.Faraday's observation cuts straight to a basic truth about human nature. The quote reminds us that total self-righteousness is far more dangerous than simple ignorance. Someone who knows they do not have all the answers will stop to look at new evidence. Someone who believes they hold the absolute truth feels no need to listen, check facts, or hold back.The origins of this quote belong to a scientist who spent his life fighting against easy assumptions. Born in 1791 to a poor blacksmith in London, Michael Faraday received very little basic schooling. He learned science while working as a bookbinder's apprentice, reading the pages he was hired to stitch together.Through hard work, he earned a job as an assistant to chemist Humphry Davy at the Royal Institution.Faraday went on to discover electromagnetic induction, invent the basic electric motor, and discover benzene.Despite his massive success in physics and chemistry, Faraday remained humble about human knowledge. He was a devoted member of the Sandemanian church, a small Christian group that emphasized humility and the limits of human wisdom. In his science talks during the 1840s and 1850s, Faraday often warned other researchers not to fall in love with their own ideas.While the exact words appear across different letters, journals, and accounts of his talks, Faraday regularly shared this main point: the most dangerous mind in a laboratory is one that has stopped doubting itself.Philosophers and psychologists have long studied why fixed certainty causes so much damage. In the 1990s, psychologists David Dunning and Justin Kruger published landmark research on human thinking, showing that people with limited knowledge in a subject often overestimate their own skill. This phenomenon, known as the Dunning-Kruger effect, shows that confidence often peaks before real understanding even begins.From a philosophical view, Faraday’s warning matches the ideas of Karl Popper, a 20th-century thinker. Popper argued that real science depends on testing ideas to see if they can be proven wrong. A real scientific theory must always stay open to new facts.When a person loses the ability to accept that they might be mistaken, they stop using reason and start following blind belief. History shows that when absolute certainty combines with political, religious, or ideological power, the results are usually terrible. Strict regimes, historical trials, and sudden financial crashes all rely on leaders who are completely convinced of their own correctness.Today, Faraday's warning applies far beyond science labs. Modern digital platforms are built on tools that reward anger and extreme views over thoughtful debate. Online spaces often act as echo chambers, surrounding people with opinions that only confirm what they already believe.This creates leaders, managers, and public figures who refuse to change their minds when conditions shift. In business, major company failures usually trace back to bosses who were completely sure of their plans, ignoring early warnings and feedback from their workers. In health care, government policy, and personal life, a complete refusal to admit doubt stops learning and cuts off teamwork.In contrast, healthy teams depend on what modern workplace psychologists call psychological safety and intellectual humility. Groups perform much better when people can openly say "I do not know" or "I was wrong."Michael Faraday’s entire career succeeded because he refused to believe that existing science had found all the answers. When top scientists believed electricity and magnetism were completely separate, Faraday stayed curious, ran hundreds of failed experiments, and finally proved they were connected.Shortly before his death in 1867, Faraday wrote a letter about his desire to keep his mind free of rigid bias. He understood that knowledge is not a fixed wall, but an ongoing process of testing ideas against real-world facts.Holding onto a healthy sense of doubt is not a sign of weakness. It is a necessary tool for survival, keeping people open to new facts, better ideas, and the simple truth that none of us know everything.
Article Summary: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction, invent the basic electric motor, and discover benzene. Faraday’s entire career succeeded because he refused to believe that existing science had found all the answers. A real scientific theory must always stay open to new facts.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg is not convinced if OpenAI and Anthropic really want Chinese AI models in America, says: Signal is ...
Article Text:
The increasing Chinese competition



Open vs closed models



Mark Zuckerberg makes an offer to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei



Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has entered the intensifying Washington debate over whether Chinese AI models should be restricted in the US, wanting that banning them would not be ‘an effective solution’. In an interview with Financial Times, Zuckerberg said the US should compete by identifying bottlenecks and roadblocks rather than blocking rivals outright. He also cautioned against ‘regulatory capture’ by American frontier labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic, which he suggested could use policy to throttle domestic competition. Zuckerberg’s remarks appeared to be a broadside against OpenAI and Anthropic, which dominate the chatbot market with proprietary closed models. He said there were “mixed signals” about whether frontier labs truly want open-source models to succeed. “Are the frontier labs going to want an open-source model to succeed? I think that there have kind of been some mixed signals on that,” he told the FT.The comments from Zuckerberg comes after Beijing-based Moonsht AI released its Kimi K3 model, whose capabilities are nearing those of OpenAI and Anthropic. US officials have also accused Moonshot of covertly training its model using distillation from American rivals, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warning that sanctions are on the table for labs that cross into intellectual property theft.Zuckerberg reiterated his support for “AI for everyone” and open models that users can customize and run on their own hardware — a popular approach among Chinese developers. He warned that AI risks becoming centralized in the hands of a few powerful groups. While Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called for stronger regulation and Google DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis has proposed a self-regulatory body, Zuckerberg said restrictions on powerful tools were not the right answer. He argued that open models could help patch cybersecurity vulnerabilities faster than closed ones.Zuckerberg’s intervention highlights a growing split among U.S. tech leaders over how to respond to Chinese competition and regulate AI. While rivals push for tighter controls, he is positioning Meta as a champion of open-source approaches — even as his company develops its own closed model, Muse Spark, citing safety concerns.In related news, recently it was reported that Meta is in early talks to lease computing power to Anthropic in a deal that could be worth as much as $10 billion over two years, according to a New York Times report. If it closes, it would hand Mark Zuckerberg a brand-new line of business and pull Dario Amodei's AI lab deeper into a scramble for compute that shows no sign of easing.The move borrows straight from Elon Musk's playbook. Musk turned SpaceX's Colossus data centers into a rental business earlier this year, and Anthropic became its anchor tenant. Now Zuckerberg wants a slice of the same action, using the very data centers his investors keep grumbling about. Anthropic pitched the idea first, in JuneThe NYT reports that Anthropic proposed the deal in June, and Meta is weighing it. Anthropic would pay in monthly instalments across two years, with either side free to opt out early. The specifics are still moving around.
Article Summary: Zuckerberg says US should compete by identifying bottlenecks and roadblocks rather than blocking rivals outright. Warns against ‘regulatory capture’ by American frontier labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic, which he suggested could use policy to throttle domestic competition.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Bob Ross: 'The very fact that you're aware of suffering is enough reason to...' and the darkest secret behind human happiness
Article Text:
Robert Norman Ross was an American painter and art instructor

“The very fact that you're aware of suffering is enough reason to be overjoyed that you're alive and can experience it.”

The quiet studio on public television

The Joy of Painting

Simple philosophy in a denim shirt

Living mindfully in a fast world

Standing in front of a wet canvas on television, a soft-spoken painter in a denim shirt painted a stroke of dark brown paint onto a bright landscape. He looked directly into the camera and offered a quiet thought:The sentence sounds strange when you first hear it. Society usually treats pain as a problem—something to fix, hide, or cure with medicine. Yet Bob Ross points to a simple truth about human life. Pain is not a sign that our body or mind is broken. It is proof that we are alive and processing the world. Experiencing heartbreak, grief, or frustration requires an active mind. The pain itself may hurt, but the ability to feel it belongs only to the living.Bob Ross spoke those words during an episode of, the public television show he hosted from 1983 to 1994. Filmed at a small TV station in Muncie, Indiana, US, the show had a low budget, but Ross reached millions of viewers with his gentle voice and simple painting style.The story behind his comment was deeply personal. Ross was grieving the loss of his second wife, Jane, who had died of cancer in 1992. On camera, Ross rarely talked about his personal sad news.He kept his focus on "happy little trees" and soft clouds. In this specific episode, however, he talked about why dark paint is necessary on a canvas to make the light colors show up.He moved naturally from art tips to human emotions. He explained that life follows the same rules as a painting. Without dark moments, the good moments lose their brightness. Ross was not a college professor giving a lecture. He was an art instructor sharing a lesson learned through personal loss, speaking to an audience of late-night viewers, elderly people at home, and tired insomniacs.The logic behind Ross’s words matches ideas from ancient Stoic thinkers and modern philosophers. The ancient teacher Epictetus taught that human beings cannot control outside events, only their own reaction to them. Noticing pain without letting it destroy you is a key part of this ancient mindset.In the mid-twentieth century, psychiatrist Viktor Frankl explained a similar idea in his 1946 book Man’s Search for Meaning. Writing about his survival in Nazi concentration camps, Frankl observed that suffering is an unavoidable part of life, just like death. Without struggle and loss, human life cannot be complete. Frankl argued that when a person cannot change a painful situation, they are forced to change themselves. Recognizing pain becomes the first step toward finding purpose.In terms of psychology, Ross was describing how human senses notice contrast. The brain understands life through comparison. Constant happiness leads to a state where nothing feels special anymore, something psychologists call sensory adaptation. Pain resets our baseline expectations. The sharp sting of loss makes quiet moments of safety and love feel much sweeter.Ross’s point is especially helpful today in a world focused on quick comfort, digital distractions, and instant fixes. Modern culture often treats emotional distress as a personal failure or a technical problem. When human sadness is treated like a bug that needs to be deleted, people lose the ability to deal with basic life struggles.In modern mental health therapy, doctors use a technique called radical acceptance. Created by psychologist Marsha Linehan, this approach teaches people that deep suffering comes from trying to fight or ignore reality. Accepting grief or physical pain as a basic fact of life helps people stay grounded in the present moment instead of panicking about their discomfort.This perspective also changes how people handle failure at work or in life. An athlete healing from an injury or a business owner facing a failed project can view their disappointment as proof that they tried hard. Feeling sad about a loss simply means the goal mattered to you.Ross recorded more than 400 episodes of his show, creating thousands of landscape paintings that were stored in cardboard boxes at his company's office in Herndon, Virginia. He died of lymphoma in 1995 at the age of 52. His paintings remain largely unsold, but the simple mindset he shared next to his easel continues to give people a practical guide for handling all the ups and downs of life.
Article Summary: Bob Ross was an American painter and art instructor. He was grieving the loss of his second wife, Jane, who had died of cancer in 1992. Ross recorded more than 400 episodes of his show, creating thousands of landscape paintings. He died of lymphoma in 1995 at the age of 52.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: How to get your CIBIL credit score without a PAN card
Article Text:
Your credit score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity.

What is a CIBIL score?

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

CIBIL credit score : Understanding your creditworthiness is pivotal in today's financial landscape, especially when seeking loans or credit cards. The Credit Information Bureau (India) Limited, commonly known as CIBIL, plays an important role in this regard by providing credit scores to borrowers.According to ET, credit score helps banks make informed decisions about extending credit cards and loans. Your credit history influences your CIBIL score , which is calculated using a special method.Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.1. Go to the official CIBIL website and click on 'Personal CIBIL score,' then 'Get Your Free CIBIL score.' Follow the link provided and fill in all the required details.2. If you don’t have a PAN Card, you can use an alternative identification such as Passport, Voter ID, Driver’s License, or Ration Card. Enter the number of the chosen ID.3. Provide your date of birth, PIN code, and select your state. Finally, enter your mobile number and click on ‘Accept and Continue’.4. Authenticate your identity by entering the OTP (One-Time Password) delivered to your mobile device on the next screen. Click 'Continue' to proceed.5. Choose whether you want to link the device with your account. Select 'Yes' or 'No' based on your preference.6. Upon successful registration, you will see a page confirming that 'You have successfully registered!'7. Click on ‘Go to Dashboard’ to access and view your CIBIL score.The factors influencing the new CIBIL score, as stated on the CIBIL website, include:1. Depth of credit: This refers to the duration of your existing credit history, calculated from the opening date of your oldest credit account.2. Long-term trend of outstanding balances: The overall trend of outstanding balances over time affects your score.3. Transaction history on credit cards: How you manage transactions on your credit cards impacts your score.4. Ratio of actual repayment amount to total amount due: This ratio indicates your repayment behavior and influences your score accordingly.5. Number of new accounts opened and number of accounts closed: Opening or closing accounts can affect your score, so managing these actions wisely is important.
Article Summary: Your CIBIL score is a three-digit number that reflects your creditworthiness and repayment capacity. Ranging from 300 to 900, a higher score indicates a stronger likelihood of loan approval. Banks and financial institutions use this score to assess the risk associated with lending money.

Article Title: Can ICE or CBP read your deleted messages: Here's what US Customs and Border Protection can and cannot do with your electronic devices at airports
Article Text:
AI generated image for representation

“Can ICE or CBP read your deleted messages? The answer is yes,”

What CBP can do with electronic devices at airports



Basic search: Officers may review information stored on a device without requiring reasonable suspicion.

Advanced search: Officers may connect external equipment to copy or analyse a device's contents, but only when there is reasonable suspicion of a violation of laws enforced by CBP or a national security concern. Advanced searches also require supervisory approval.

What CBP cannot do during a border search



Can CBP recover deleted messages



ICE and CBP follow different policies



A recent Instagram video by immigration attorney Deepak Ahluwalia has raised questions about whether US border officials can recover deleted messages from travellers' phones during airport inspections. In the video, Ahluwalia claims that a client entering the US through San Francisco International Airport had permanently deleted messages that were recovered and reviewed during an inspection by US Customs and Border Protection (CBP).Ahluwalia said in the video. He added that, according to the client, CBP officers recovered messages that were not linked to any cloud service and had been permanently deleted, and that those messages were later used in deciding the individual's entry into the US. However, CBP's policy does not specifically state whether deleted messages can be recovered during a border search, but it does outline what officers are permitted and not permitted to do when examining electronic devices.Under CBP's Border Search of Electronic Devices directive, officers may inspect electronic devices, including mobile phones, tablets, laptops, smartwatches, cameras, and storage devices, as part of border inspections conducted when people enter or leave the US. The searches are intended to support customs, immigration, law enforcement and homeland security responsibilities. The directive allows officers to conduct two types of searches:CBP may also request that travellers unlock their devices or provide passcodes to facilitate an inspection.If officers cannot inspect a passcode-protected or encrypted device, they may detain it while determining how to proceed.The directive also places limits on electronic device searches. According to the policy, officers may not intentionally access information stored solely remotely, such as data stored only in cloud storage. To avoid accessing remote information, officers are instructed to ask travellers to place devices in airplane mode and disable Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, or disable network connectivity themselves when necessary.The directive further states that passcodes obtained during an inspection may be used only to inspect the device and the information stored on it. They cannot be used to access information that exists only remotely, and any recorded passcodes should be deleted or destroyed once they are no longer needed for the search.CBP's directive does not specifically address whether officers can recover permanently deleted messages from electronic devices or whether forensic tools may be used to do so.However, the policy permits advanced searches involving external equipment to analyse device contents when legal requirements are met, and it also allows CBP to seek technical assistance if a device is encrypted or otherwise not readily accessible.Because the directive does not explicitly discuss deleted messages, it does not confirm or deny whether such information can be recovered during a border inspection.The directive also notes that it applies to searches conducted by CBP. Searches performed by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), including Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), are governed by ICE's own policies and procedures. If CBP transfers a device or copied information to HSI for further analysis, ICE policies apply after HSI receives the device or information.
Article Summary: US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) searches electronic devices at airports. CBP's policy does not specifically state whether deleted messages can be recovered during a border search, but it does outline what officers are permitted and not permitted to do when examining electronic devices.

Article Title: How AI Czar David Sacks 'predicted' what Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said on Chinese open-weights models
Article Text:
David Sacks predicted Anthropic’s messaging shift



“Nobody is trying to ban open source.”

“We just want to limit who can use it.”

“We just want to limit who can contribute to it.”

“We just want to limit how powerful those models can be.”

“We just want to make sure the guardrails (we lobbied for) can’t be removed.”

“The net effect will be the same. They won’t stop until they kneecap open source. The rest of the industry needs to watch these guys like a hawk.”

Anthropic outlines alternative guardrails



Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pushed back against industry criticism, insisting that his company has “never advocated for a ban on open-weights models”. The statement comes as tech leaders and former White House AI advisor David Sacks debate whether closed-model AI labs are attempting to restrict open-source technology under the guise of safety.Amodei’s comments have been published in a company blog post following an open letter released late last week by a coalition of major tech companies, including Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta and Palantir, urging policymakers to avoid placing “premature restrictions” on open-weight AI models. While chief rival OpenAI eventually added its support to the coalition’s letter, Anthropic declined to sign.The pushback from Amodei is exactly what Sacks posted two days ago (on July 26) with warnings that Anthropic will attempt to “kneecap open source” through targeted lobbying. Sacks said that Anthropic would attempt to reframe its regulatory push to avoid a public backlash while still restricting open-weight developments:“The entire tech industry (save for Anthropic) has come out in favor of open source AI. So what happens next? Will Anthropic change its lobbying efforts? Not likely. Now the gaslighting begins,” he said. Sacks wrote a bunch of points that Anthropic would say on the issue:He said thatIn his blog post, Amodei denied seeking a blanket ban on open-weight software, which allows users to download, modify and run models locally on their own infrastructure. Instead, he argued that national security and safety efforts should focus on hardware access, data scraping and rigorous pre-release evaluations:“To summarize my and Anthropic’s position, we have not and are not advocating for a ban on open-weights models as a category. We should instead focus on keeping powerful chips out of authoritarian hands, stopping industrial-scale distillation, and requiring safety testing of all sufficiently capable models, open and closed,” Amodei wrote.
Article Summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei pushed back against industry criticism, insisting that his company has “never advocated for a ban on open-weights models” The statement comes as tech leaders and former White House AI advisor David Sacks debate whether closed-model AI labs are attempting to restrict open-source technology under the guise of safety.

Article Title: T-Mobile outage: Company says service restored, read full statement
Article Text:
What is ‘SOS’ or ‘SOS only’ means



T-Mobile has said that it has fully restored network service after a widespread outage that left tens of thousands of US customers without cellular signal or mobile internet. The disruption began around 4:00 p.m. ET on July 27, causing reports to surge on tracking platform Downdetector. At its peak, more than 62,000 incidents were logged nationwide, with users across several states, including California, Georgia, Arizona and Utah, reporting that their phones were stuck in “SOS” mode.“We have fully restored service for all customers and sincerely apologize for the difficulties to those who experienced network impacts today,” the wireless carrier said in a post on X (formerly Twitter), adding, “At @TMobile, we know that customers rely on us to stay connected to what matters most, and we appreciate their understanding as we prioritised resolution.”Users complained that their phones displayed “SOS” or “SOS only”. This means that the device has lost connection to its primary cellular network, though emergency calls can still be placed. During the peak of the disruption, T-Mobile acknowledged the issue and stated that resolving the technical challenges was its highest priority:“Our teams are actively working on the reports of technical challenges impacting some customers.Any service impacts are in the process of being resolved and are our highest priority. We know how critical it is to stay connected and every available resource is focused on resolving this as quickly as possible,” the company said in a statement on X. T-Mobile did not immediately provide a specific cause for the technical glitch.According to Downdetector data, the majority of user-submitted complaints focused on mobile phone connections, complete loss of signal and failing mobile internet access.Minor spikes in outage reports were also noted by users of other major networks during the same timeframe, including around 1,000 reports for Verizon and 850 for AT&T, which often occurs when subscribers attempt to place cross-network calls to an affected provider.
Article Summary: T-Mobile has said that it has fully restored network service after a widespread outage. The disruption began around 4:00 p.m. ET on July 27, causing reports to surge on tracking platform Downdetector. At its peak, more than 62,000 incidents were logged nationwide.

Article Title: As iPhone 18 series launch nears, the price of staying loyal to Apple is rising
Article Text:
Apple is expected to bring iPhone 18 series later this year in September

Apple premium is getting pricier

iPhone is an outlier, but may not be for long

Every Apple user eventually gets an offer they can't refuse: buy another Apple product. An iPhone leads to AirPods, which leads to a Mac, then an Apple Watch, iCloud, Apple Music and AppleCare+. The ecosystem has always been designed to pull users deeper in. Now it's asking them to pay more at every step. There was a time when buying into the Apple ecosystem meant paying a premium once and then enjoying the benefits of seamless integration across devices and services. That premium was never small, but it was relatively predictable.That equation is changing. Over the past month, Apple has quietly raised prices across almost every part of its ecosystem — hardware, extended warranties and subscription services. Some increases are being blamed on soaring memory prices, others on higher music licensing costs, while currency movements have driven hikes in markets such as Japan. The reasons differ, but the outcome is the same: staying inside Apple's ecosystem is becoming steadily more expensive.The June hardware price increases were the biggest signal. Macs and iPads saw sharp revisions after Apple cited unprecedented increases in DRAM and NAND flash memory costs.The company said the explosion of AI infrastructure globally has created intense demand for high-bandwidth memory, squeezing supply and raising component prices. The impact was significant.The MacBook Air, long considered Apple's most accessible premium laptop, now starts at Rs 1,49,900 instead of Rs 1,19,900. The 15-inch model moved to Rs 1,79,900. The entry-level iPad climbed to Rs 44,900, while the iPad Air and iPad Pro also became substantially costlier. Even refurbished products, traditionally Apple's value proposition for budget-conscious buyers, are no longer insulated from these increases.The ripple effect is visible beyond computers and tablets. AppleCare+ subscriptions for Macs and iPads now cost more. Existing subscribers have been protected, but anyone buying a new device will pay higher monthly or annual charges simply to insure it. Then came services.Apple Music now costs more, with Apple explicitly pointing to rising licensing costs. Apple One Family and Premier bundles have also become more expensive. Individually, these increases appear modest. Collectively, they raise the cost of remaining fully invested in Apple's ecosystem.This is where Apple's pricing strategy becomes interesting. Unlike many consumer electronics companies that depend largely on one-time hardware sales, Apple increasingly earns recurring revenue from services. Hardware brings customers into the ecosystem; subscriptions keep them there.Apple's ecosystem has always worked like a beautifully designed trap. You don't notice it closing until you're already inside. By then, your photos are in iCloud, your music is on Apple Music, you can’t go a day without checking those three rings on the Watch, and your AirPods jump between devices with so much ease that you never, ever think about any other wireless earbuds.Higher recurring fees therefore have an outsized impact. A customer who buys a Mac, an iPhone and an iPad is no longer paying only for devices. They are paying every month for storage, entertainment, warranties and bundled services. Even Apple's accessories illustrate the growing premium.The AirPods Max, ridiculously priced at Rs 67,900, remain among the most expensive mainstream wireless headphones despite increasing competition from Sony, Bose and Sennheiser . Their appeal lies less in audio quality alone than in how effortlessly they integrate with iPhones, Macs and iPads through automatic device switching, spatial audio and Apple's broader ecosystem. That convenience, however, now carries an increasingly steep price tag. For many consumers, the biggest question is what happens nextThe iPhone has so far escaped a global price increase, although Japan recently saw prices rise by up to 11%. That move was largely attributed to currency fluctuations, but it also shows Apple is willing to recalibrate prices market by market when conditions demand it. The more significant test will come later this year.Industry watchers increasingly expect Apple's next iPhone lineup to launch at higher prices as elevated component costs continue to pressure margins. Unlike memory shortages of previous cycles, today's constraints are closely linked to AI infrastructure spending, suggesting they may persist for longer.If iPhone prices rise, the psychological impact could be considerable. The smartphone remains the anchor product around which Apple's ecosystem revolves. A higher entry price could also make upgrading less frequent, pushing more consumers towards financing schemes, trade-in programmes and certified refurbished devices.Then there is the foldable iPhone. Whenever Apple launches its first foldable device (expected in September), it is unlikely to compete on affordability. Given the cost of foldable displays, complex hinge mechanisms and Apple's traditional premium positioning, the device could comfortably become the most expensive iPhone the company has ever sold in India, potentially redefining the upper end of the smartphone market.None of this appears accidental. Apple has spent years transforming itself from a hardware company into an ecosystem company. Once customers own multiple Apple devices, subscribe to several services and rely on ecosystem-specific features, price sensitivity naturally declines. That gives Apple more room than most competitors to pass on higher costs without dramatically affecting loyalty.Whether that strategy continues to work depends on how much consumers value integration over affordability. Apple continues to offer one of the most polished technology ecosystems available. But as hardware, services, warranties and accessories all move higher together, the cost of belonging is climbing faster than ever.The Apple ecosystem still delivers convenience. The question is whether that convenience is becoming a luxury that fewer consumers are willing to keep paying for.
Article Summary: Apple has quietly raised prices across almost every part of its ecosystem. Some increases are being blamed on soaring memory prices, others on higher music licensing costs, while currency movements have driven hikes in markets such as Japan. AppleCare+ subscriptions for Macs and iPads now cost more.

Article Title: Microsoft unveils Project Perception and MAI-Cyber-1-Flash; claims new cybersecurity AI model beats Gemini and GPT on vulnerability detection while cutting costs by 50%

"The physics of cybersecurity are changing. Autonomous systems can now reason, adapt and operate continuously. At the same time, the cost of offence is falling, while the volume, velocity and complexity of what must be secured continues to grow."

Microsoft has unveiled Project Perception, a new agentic cybersecurity system, alongside MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, its first AI model built specifically for software vulnerability analysis. The company claims that the new cybersecurity model outperforms Gemini and GPT on vulnerability-detection benchmarks while reducing operational costs by 50%.The announcements come as Microsoft says AI is changing the pace and scale of cyberattacks, requiring security teams to move beyond traditional approaches. According to the company, MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, when integrated into its multi-agent vulnerability identification and remediation system (MDASH), achieved 96% on the CyberGym benchmark, outperforming Mythos, Gemini and GPT-based configurations while lowering costs compared with its current deployment.Project Perception is Microsoft's new agentic security system designed to help organisations continuously identify, assess and reduce cyber risks across their digital environments.The platform coordinates three specialised categories of AI agents:Microsoft said the system combines security signals, threat intelligence, AI models and autonomous agents into a continuous workflow that helps organisations move from reactive incident response to ongoing risk reduction.Alongside Project Perception, Microsoft introduced MAI-Cyber-1-Flash, describing it as its first cybersecurity-specialised AI model. The compact model has been developed for software vulnerability analysis and forms part of Microsoft's broader multi-model strategy, which combines specialised AI models with larger frontier models depending on the security task.According to Microsoft, MAI-Cyber-1-Flash handles approximately 90% of software vulnerability analysis tasks, allowing larger AI models to be reserved for more complex cases.The company said the combined MDASH with MAI-Cyber-1-Flash configuration achieved 96% on CyberGym, which it described as an industry benchmark for evaluating how AI systems identify vulnerabilities across large software codebases. Microsoft added that the result was 12 percentage points higher than Mythos and ahead of Gemini and GPT-based systems while delivering 50% lower costs than its current MDASH configuration.Microsoft said Project Perception is built on what it calls a New Cyber Stack, consisting of six layers:According to the company, these layers work together to collect security signals across identities, endpoints, cloud services, applications, data and AI systems before transforming them into context that AI agents can use to identify risks and recommend or take corrective actions.Microsoft said the system uses a multi-model architecture that selects different AI models based on factors including quality, reliability, latency and cost instead of relying on a single model for every cybersecurity task.Microsoft said Project Perception will enter public preview on August 3.
